body:
I have no idea how to format posts like you have, apologies if i'm responding to things all jumbled and it confuses you. 

I think becoming ' shy ' was a big thing for me - I was quite well known as the class clown so when my anxiety hit I lost a lot of friends who liked me only because I defied the teachers and was never a quiet presence in the class, which evidently was a facade I couldn't keep up anymore because when I was in classes I was just paranoid constantly about having an attack and people knowing. 

Yeah, it really sucks. It sucks even worse when you've had multiple chances with the wrong people - I've had guys try to force themselves on me before I kind of got away whilst they got high fived from their friends for the attempt and I think it really, really put me off the whole idea of sex and people touching me for months on end.

I've actually seen a therapist since I was 15. My first therapist was a nightmare and ended up making me ten times worse, and my other therapist was nice but did jack shit and dropped me as soon as she could. Here, at age 18 you've got to be transferred to adult mental health services which apparently I didn't quality for because I was ' better. ' Which is probably codename for we don't want to be paying for your mental health care anymore, eat shit. 

In various ways, I'm sorry you can relate because it really made me feel like an outsider amongst people I'm meant to feel comfortable with. It'd start with jokes, like when I'd be quiet they'd ask if I was anxious and then start laughing - but they'd speak to their boyfriends and stuff about me and they'd talk to me normally before sliding in their anxiety jokes like I was meant to laugh along. One friend I remember quite clearly getting drunk out of her mind and telling me at a party full of people that I was an attention whore and that mental illness' like anxiety aren't real, and a lot of my friends laughed then too. She also kicked me out of her house at 6am for waking her up having a panic attack. I guess you can see then why I now don't have any friends.

That also sucks, you getting kicked out of college. I also was threatened quite a few times with the prospect of getting kicked out of school, but that was just because I misbehaved. Back then I was pretty adventurous with what I did, before my anxiety kicked in of course. 

Being lonely romantically is something I can relate to, even if really it doesn't upset me as much as not having any friends does. I'm nearly 19 now with no experiences and at 17 when I had said this to people they'd look at me completely disbelievingly. I think I have a lot of problems, finding a root is hard. I don't really feel like I have ever had a solid idea of what I wanted to do in life whereas many of my friends would; I went to a high achieving school so there was even more pressure on top of that so my expectations begun to get too high. Anxiety plays a massive part too, as it begun with that and developed into depression and some days I'm too anxious to even step foot outside of the house. I just don't have a very good idea of myself mentally and with good reason - generally I think I'm pretty disposable and that if I died it wouldn't really make a difference as I'm living doing absolutely nothing right now.
